title: BS-PDN-Last: Towards Optimal Power Delivery Network Design With Multifunctional Backside Metal Layers
problem: Backside metal layers in advanced chips can serve multiple functions (power delivery, signal routing, thermal); traditional PDN-first design flows reserve these layers for power, leaving suboptimal signal routing and performance trade-offs.
motivation: Maximizing PPA (power, performance, area) gains with multifunctional backside requires rethinking the physical design order; conventional flows constrain the design space.
method: BS-PDN-last flow defers power routing to the post-signal routing stage, allowing signal routing to optimize for performance first, then power delivery networks to adapt to remaining backside resources. Uses vector-based IR-drop analysis for accurate power estimation.
key_novelty: Deferring power delivery network design to post-signal routing stage to unlock multifunctional backside utilization and optimize performance-power trade-offs.
contributions: BS-PDN-last design flow achieving 90% reduction in Total Negative Slack
12% performance gain with backside current distribution network (BS-CDN)
First comprehensive comparison of FS-PDN, BS-PDN, and multifunctional backside designs with vector-based analysis

metrics.other: 90% reduction in Total Negative Slack, 12% performance gain with BS-CDN
